## Approach

This lab is asking to use the API 's from NobelPrize.org and answer 4 data-driven questions using those API's. To first use the NobelPrize APi's an API key is not required so I will not have to create an environ file to store my key and secret. The packages I will use to pull and tidy Nobel Prize data I anticipate using the HTTR2, the TIdyr and the JSONLite packages. All these packages have methods that I can use to read the Nobel Prize data, convert it from a JSON object into a data structure and clean and tidy the data set. The endpoints that I plan on using are the Laureate and Prize.

### Data-Driven Questions:

\
1. Which Country lost the most Nobel laureates?

-   I plan on using the filter() method to only include results where the bornCountry and the Country columns are different. Then I will create a summary table to count which country has lost the most Nobel laureates

\
2. Was there was a increase in the loss of laureates during the times of WW1(1914 - 1918) and WW2 (1939 - 1945)

-   I will use my previous filter results from question 1, and filter those results by years and count the total amount of observations between those years. I will also create a graph to show the amount of "lost laureates" every year to track if there were any trends during that time

3\. Out of all the US laureates what category do US winners share the largest percentage of?

-   I will take the data set, filter for only US citizens and calculate the proportion for each category. I will likely use a bar graph to visualize this data.

4\. What country has won the most Nobel Prizes?

-   I will take the data set and create a summary table to count the amount of nobel prize winners.

## Code Base

```{r load-packages}
library(httr2)
library(jsonlite)
library(tidyr)

```

```{r API-call}
req <- request("http://api.nobelprize.org/v1/laureate.json?gender=All")
resp <- req_perform(req)
nobel_data <- resp_body_json(resp)

nobel_df <- nobel_data$laureates %>% 
  tibble(laureates = .) %>%
  unnest_wider(laureates)

nobel_df <- nobel_df %>% mutate(
  born = as.Date(born)
)

nobel_df <- nobel_df %>% mutate(
  died = as.Date(died)
)

nobel_df <- nobel_df %>% 
 unnest_longer(prizes)

nobel_df<- nobel_df %>%
  unnest_wider(prizes)

nobel_df<- nobel_df %>%
  unnest_longer(affiliations)

nobel_df<- nobel_df %>%
  unnest_wider(affiliations)

nobel_df <- nobel_df %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(year))

```

## What country has lost the most Laureates?

```{r most-lost-laureates}
#Filter for laureates with another country
lost_laureates <- nobel_df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(bornCountryCode),
    !is.na(country),
    bornCountry != country
  )

#Count unique laureates by birth conuntry
country_losses <- lost_laureates %>%
  group_by(bornCountry) %>%
  summarise(
    total_lost = n_distinct(id),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_lost))

country_losses

#The country with the most losses
country_losses %>%
  slice_max(total_lost, n = 1)




```

```{r loss-laureates-visualization}
country_losses %>%
  slice_max(total_lost, n = 10) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(bornCountry, total_lost),
             y = total_lost)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Countries by Nobel Laureate Loss",
    x = "Country of Birth",
    y = "Number of Laureates"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

It seems that the United Kingdom has lost the most laureates based on this data. However, it is worth noting that the loss of laureates is calculated inaccurately if modern borders are considered. For example, Germany comes in 2nd place with 21 lost laureates but West Germany and Prussia have 5 and 4 lost laureates respectively and both countries are considered part of Germany now, so if those are counted together than Germany would have more lost laureates than the United Kingdom.

## Did the loss of laureates increase during World War I and World War II?

```{r count-laureates}
loss_by_year <- lost_laureates %>%
  distinct(id, year) %>%
  count(year, name = "total_lost") %>%
  arrange(year)

war_losses <- lost_laureates %>%
  mutate(
    period = case_when(
      year >= 1914 & year <= 1918 ~ "World War I",
      year >= 1939 & year <= 1945 ~ "World War II",
      TRUE ~ "Other Years"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  summarise(
    total_laureates = n_distinct(id),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

war_losses
```

```{r losses-over-time}
ggplot(loss_by_year, aes(x = year, y = total_lost)) +
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = 1914, xmax = 1918,
    ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
    fill = "blue", alpha = 0.15
  ) +
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = 1939, xmax = 1945,
    ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
    fill = "red", alpha = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_line(color = "black") +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Internationally Affiliated Nobel Laureates by Year",
    subtitle = "Blue: WWI | Red: WWII",
    x = "Prize Year",
    y = "Number of Laureates"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Out of all Laureates, which category accounts for the largest percentage?

```{r us-laureates}
us_laureates <- nobel_df %>%
  filter(bornCountryCode == "US")

us_categories <- us_laureates %>%
  distinct(id, category) %>%
  count(category, name = "total") %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = round(total / sum(total) * 100, 2)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(percentage))

us_categories

ggplot(us_categories,
       aes(x = reorder(category, percentage),
           y = percentage)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of US-Born Nobel Laureates by Category",
    x = "Nobel Prize Category",
    y = "Percentage (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

us_categories %>%
  slice_max(percentage, n = 1)
```

The data shows that about 28.33% of all laureates given to a United States citizen were in the medicine category.

## What country has won the most Nobel Prizes?

```{r most-nobel-prizes}
nobel_df %>%
  count(bornCountry, sort=TRUE)

```

The United States has won the most Nobel Prizes with 299 prizes.
